scope: General bounded serial java.util.concurrent and Java Thread compatibility, no package/profile/module bypass. Dedicated BackgroundWorkers transport is required for successful Thread.start/execute.

basis.implementation: Independent Rust implementation from public API contracts; no JDK implementation source copied.

observed_blocker.result: Actual prior NRO failure, not proof that this new implementation runs on Horizon.

implementation.pool: Supports core=max=1, TimeUnit.SECONDS, initialized LinkedBlockingQueue and supplied ThreadFactory. First command belongs directly to the new worker; subsequent accepted commands are observable in getQueue() and FIFO. Idle timeout measures monotonic time; later execute creates a new factory Thread. Graceful shutdown drains accepted work and rejects later submissions.
implementation.roots: Live transport tokens root Java Threads; Thread target, pool, factory, queue, first/running/queued jobs and pending exception objects participate in GC. Temporary factory roots use unique scope tickets, so separate native workers can release VmGate and resume/unwind out of order without removing another worker scope.
implementation.threads: Real standalone Thread targets and virtual subclass.run execute once on dedicated platform workers. Actual active NativeHost owner maps to the Java Thread object through final TLS cleanup; Interpreter fallback uses active invocation identity only. Names are Java metadata, not a claim of OS-thread naming.
implementation.namespace: Thread/executor tokens reserve bit62; Timer tokens are hard-bounded below bit62. Generic Android background_worker_step/stopped/error route by namespace. Counters never reuse live token identities.
implementation.factory: Actually invokes custom ThreadFactory.newThread, preserves returned Thread object/Java name/unchanged Runnable, and validates NEW/base run/start behavior before OS start or command acceptance. Null, replaced/wrapped worker target, overridden pool run/start and reentrant worker creation fail explicitly.
implementation.bounds: 32 live Java Thread workers,128 records per object family including pending-error admission,4096 queue elements in total plus at most one initial command per live worker,4096-byte requested Thread names. Platform limits can be lower and fail explicitly.
implementation.errors: Failed start/wake leaves command unaccepted. Exact uncaught task, VM or platform error follows shared app-fatal policy; failed tasks are not counted completed. Pending job roots remain until real worker stop. No custom uncaught-handler or replacement-worker recovery claim.

coverage: Default/custom factory dispatch, real returned Thread identity/name, worker-only execution and graceful FIFO drain in two package names.
Keep-alive expiry at exact monotonic deadline; subsequent submission creates a new token and invokes factory again.
Null/wrong-target/overridden-worker/throwing factory and backend start/wake failures reject before acceptance.
Unsupported pool/interrupt APIs fail without shutdown or queue mutation.
Standalone Runnable targets and Thread subclass.run dispatch, start once, alive until actual stopped.
Queued/initial/running jobs, Thread target and pool/factory graph survive GC; roots release after real stop.
Reentrant execute+shutdown and exact uncaught ArithmeticException propagation without completed-task inflation.
Native owner changes during a suspended callback do not mislabel main Handler; Java Thread identity survives between steps through TLS cleanup.
Independent pending root scope tickets survive non-LIFO native worker completion and actual VM garbage collection.
Normal SDK proof uses actual Java VFS, currentThread, custom ThreadFactory and main Handler.
limitations: Full pool sizing/configuration, blocking queue waits, Future/submit, shutdownNow, interruption, join/await, daemon policy, ThreadGroup, priorities, OS naming and custom uncaught-handler/worker replacement are explicitly outside this bounded layer.
Pool factories with custom run/start continuations or replaced/wrapped target require resumable worker semantics and are rejected. Standalone subclass.run remains supported.
No Dynamite/Binder/analytics bypass or package exception was added.

Actual Horizon dedicated worker/concurrency/TLS behavior needs transport evidence plus a parent-run NRO-bound proof. See reports/horizon-background-workers-host-20261024.json for separate transport scope; it does not itself prove this new executor layer runs.
The JVM oracle is OpenJDK21, not an Android API26 device. No general APK/gameplay compatibility follows from host success.

shared_integration.scope: Framework attach/dispatch/roots/references/collect/pump, actual worker identity Handler/Looper restrictions, generic background callbacks and truthful builtin hierarchy/interfaces. Parent consolidated build evidence binds the full shared source graph.
